Cloud storage is a service that stores digital data on remote infrastructure and makes it accessible over a network under defined access and security controls.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a mobile app and a web app?

options.A: A mobile app is software designed to run on a mobile device; a web app is accessed through a web browser over a network
options.B: A mobile app runs in a browser; a web app is installed on a device
options.D: A mobile app is for Android only; a web app is for iOS only

questions.explanation: A mobile application is software designed to run on a mobile device such as a smartphone or tablet. A web app is accessed through a web browser over a network.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between HTTP and HTTPS?

options.A: HTTPS protects HTTP communication using TLS, helping prevent eavesdropping and tampering; HTTP by itself does not provide these protections
options.B: HTTP is secure; HTTPS is not
options.D: HTTP is for email; HTTPS is for websites

questions.explanation: HTTPS protects HTTP communication using TLS, helping prevent eavesdropping and tampering and allowing the client to authenticate the server. HTTP by itself does not provide these protections.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between data redundancy and data inconsistency?

options.A: Data redundancy is the unnecessary duplication of data; data inconsistency occurs when copies of the same data do not match
options.B: Data redundancy is when data does not match; data inconsistency is unnecessary duplication
options.D: Data redundancy is for cloud only; data inconsistency is for local only

questions.explanation: Data redundancy is the unnecessary duplication of data, which can increase storage use and cause inconsistent values if copies are not updated together. Data inconsistency occurs when copies of the same data do not match.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a hard disk drive (HDD) and a solid-state drive (SSD)?

options.A: HDD uses rotating magnetic disks and mechanical components; SSD uses flash memory
options.B: HDD uses flash memory; SSD uses magnetic disks

questions.explanation: An HDD uses rotating magnetic disks and mechanical components; an SSD uses flash memory. SSDs are generally faster and quieter, while HDDs often offer lower cost per unit of storage.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.chapter: Cyber Safety and Responsible Use of IT
questions.question: What is the difference between a Trojan horse and a worm?

options.A: A Trojan horse disguises itself as legitimate software to trick users; a worm can self-replicate and spread across systems without attaching to a host file
options.B: A Trojan horse self-replicates; a worm disguises itself
options.D: A Trojan horse is harmless; a worm is harmful

questions.explanation: A Trojan horse is malicious software that disguises itself as legitimate or useful software to trick users into installing or executing it. A worm can self-replicate and spread across systems or networks without attaching to a host file.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a website and a web page?

options.A: A website is a collection of related web pages; a web page is an individual document available on the Web
options.B: A website is a single document; a web page is a collection of websites
options.D: A website is for businesses only; a web page is for individuals only

questions.explanation: A website is a collection of related web pages and resources generally published under a common domain name. A web page is an individual document or resource available on the World Wide Web, commonly displayed in a browser.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a public cloud and a community cloud?

options.A: A public cloud is available for use by the general public or a broad group of customers; a community cloud is shared by organisations with common concerns
options.B: A public cloud is for one organisation; a community cloud is for the general public
options.D: A public cloud is always free; a community cloud is always paid

questions.explanation: A public cloud is cloud infrastructure made available for use by the general public or a broad group of customers and operated by a cloud service provider. A community cloud is cloud infrastructure shared by organisations with common concerns, such as mission, security requirements, policy or compliance needs.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a cell and a base transceiver station?

options.A: A cell is a geographic coverage area; a base transceiver station is radio access network equipment that communicates with mobile devices in its coverage area
options.B: A cell is equipment; a base transceiver station is a coverage area
options.D: A cell is for 5G only; a base transceiver station is for 2G only

questions.explanation: A cell is a geographic coverage area served by a particular base station or sector in a cellular network. A base transceiver station is radio access network equipment that communicates wirelessly with mobile devices in its coverage area.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between attenuation and noise?

options.A: Attenuation is the reduction in signal strength as it travels through a medium; noise is unwanted disturbance that can interfere with a signal
options.B: Attenuation is unwanted disturbance; noise is the reduction in signal strength
options.D: Attenuation is for wireless only; noise is for wired only

questions.explanation: Attenuation is the reduction in signal strength as it travels through a transmission medium. Noise is unwanted disturbance that can interfere with a signal and reduce the accuracy or quality of communication.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a backup and a recovery in databases?

options.A: A backup is a copy of database data for restoration; recovery is the process of restoring a database to a correct and consistent state after failure
options.B: A backup restores data; recovery creates a copy of data
options.D: A backup is for cloud only; recovery is for local only

questions.explanation: A database backup is a copy of database data and, where required, related logs or configuration information that can be used for restoration. Database recovery is the process of restoring a database to a correct and consistent state after failure, corruption or other disruption.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between an embedded computer and a general-purpose computer?

options.A: An embedded computer is built into a larger device to perform a dedicated function; a general-purpose computer is designed for multiple tasks
options.B: An embedded computer is for multiple tasks; a general-purpose computer is for a dedicated function
options.D: An embedded computer is larger than a general-purpose computer

questions.explanation: An embedded computer is a computing system built into a larger device to perform a dedicated function, such as controlling a washing machine, vehicle system or medical device. A general-purpose computer is designed for multiple tasks.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.chapter: Cyber Safety and Responsible Use of IT
questions.question: What is the difference between authentication and identification?

options.A: Identification is the process of claiming an identity; authentication is the process of verifying that identity
options.B: Identification verifies identity; authentication claims identity
options.D: Identification is for hardware; authentication is for software

questions.explanation: Identification is the process of claiming an identity, while authentication is the process of verifying the identity of a user, device or system.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between DNS and DHCP?

options.A: DNS translates domain names into IP addresses; DHCP dynamically assigns IP addresses to devices on a network
options.B: DNS assigns IP addresses; DHCP translates domain names
options.D: DNS is for email; DHCP is for websites

questions.explanation: DNS stands for Domain Name System. It translates domain names into IP addresses and provides other naming-related information. DHCP dynamically assigns IP addresses to devices on a network.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a private cloud and a hybrid cloud?

options.A: A private cloud is dedicated to a single organisation; a hybrid cloud combines two or more distinct cloud infrastructures
options.B: A private cloud combines multiple clouds; a hybrid cloud is dedicated to one organisation
options.D: A private cloud is public; a hybrid cloud is private

questions.explanation: A private cloud is cloud infrastructure provisioned for exclusive use by a single organisation. A hybrid cloud combines two or more distinct cloud infrastructures, such as private and public clouds, that remain separate but are connected to enable data or application portability.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a SIM card and an IMSI?

options.A: A SIM card is a physical or embedded module; IMSI is a unique identifier associated with a mobile subscription stored in the SIM/eSIM profile
options.B: A SIM card is an identifier; IMSI is a physical module
options.D: A SIM card is for data only; IMSI is for voice only

questions.explanation: A Subscriber Identity Module (SIM) is a secure integrated circuit or profile used to identify and authenticate a subscriber to a mobile network. IMSI stands for International Mobile Subscriber Identity, a unique identifier associated with a mobile subscription and stored in the SIM/eSIM profile.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a communication channel and a transmission medium?

options.A: A communication channel is the path through which information travels; a transmission medium is the physical or wireless path used to carry signals
options.B: A communication channel is a physical cable; a transmission medium is a logical path
options.D: A communication channel is for digital only; a transmission medium is for analog only

questions.explanation: A communication channel is the medium or path through which information travels from sender to receiver. A transmission medium is the physical or wireless path used to carry signals, such as copper cable, optical fibre or radio waves.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a query and a report in a database?

options.A: A query is a request for data or an operation on data; a report is a formatted presentation of data for a specific purpose
options.B: A query presents formatted data; a report requests data
options.D: A query is for cloud only; a report is for local only

questions.explanation: A query is a request for data or an operation on data in a database, often expressed using SQL. A report is a formatted presentation of data for a specific purpose.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a register and cache memory?

options.A: Registers are very small, high-speed storage locations inside the processor; cache is small, high-speed memory located in or close to the CPU
options.B: Registers are larger than cache; cache is inside the processor
options.D: Registers are for storage; cache is for processing

questions.explanation: Registers are very small, high-speed storage locations inside the processor used to hold instructions, addresses, data and intermediate results temporarily. Cache is small, high-speed memory located in or close to the CPU that stores frequently used instructions and data to reduce access time.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.chapter: Cyber Safety and Responsible Use of IT
questions.question: What is the difference between a secure backup and a regular backup?

options.A: A secure backup maintains protected, tested copies of important data, ideally with offline or immutable copies and restricted access; a regular backup may not have these protections
options.B: A secure backup is stored online; a regular backup is stored offline
options.D: A secure backup is for cloud only; a regular backup is for local only

questions.explanation: A secure backup practice maintains protected, tested copies of important data, ideally with offline or immutable copies and restricted access. A regular backup may not have these protections.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a hyperlink and a URL?

options.A: A hyperlink is a clickable reference that connects one web resource to another; a URL is an address used to identify and locate a resource
options.B: A hyperlink is an address; a URL is a clickable reference
options.D: A hyperlink is for email; a URL is for websites

questions.explanation: A hyperlink is a clickable reference that connects one web resource or location to another. URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator, an address used to identify and locate a resource on a network, especially the Web.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between resource pooling and rapid elasticity in cloud computing?

options.A: Resource pooling means a provider serves multiple customers using a shared pool of resources; rapid elasticity means resources can be scaled up or down quickly
options.B: Resource pooling means resources are scaled quickly; rapid elasticity means resources are shared
options.D: Resource pooling is for storage only; rapid elasticity is for computing only

questions.explanation: Resource pooling means a provider serves multiple customers using a shared pool of computing resources, with resources dynamically assigned and reassigned according to demand. Rapid elasticity means cloud resources can be scaled up or down quickly in response to changing demand.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between 1G and 2G mobile technology?

options.A: 1G used analogue technology and primarily supported voice calls; 2G introduced digital cellular communication, improving voice services and enabling text messaging
options.B: 1G supported text messaging; 2G supported voice calls only
options.D: 1G is for data only; 2G is for voice only

questions.explanation: 1G refers to the first generation of cellular networks, which used analogue technology and primarily supported voice calls. 2G refers to second-generation cellular networks that introduced digital cellular communication, improving voice services and enabling text messaging.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between multiplexing and modulation?

options.A: Multiplexing combines multiple signals for transmission over a shared channel; modulation varies a property of a carrier signal according to the information being transmitted
options.B: Multiplexing varies a carrier signal; modulation combines multiple signals
options.D: Multiplexing is for wireless only; modulation is for wired only

questions.explanation: Multiplexing combines multiple signals or data streams for transmission over a shared communication channel. Modulation is the process of varying a property of a carrier signal according to the information being transmitted.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a database index and a database view?

options.A: An index is a data structure that helps locate rows more efficiently; a view is a virtual table defined by a query
options.B: An index is a virtual table; a view is a data structure
options.D: An index is for storage; a view is for querying

questions.explanation: An index is a data structure that helps a database locate rows more efficiently, often speeding up searches at the cost of additional storage and update overhead. A view is a virtual table defined by a query; it presents selected data from one or more underlying tables.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a supercomputer and a mainframe?

options.A: A supercomputer is designed for extremely demanding calculations and simulations; a mainframe is designed to handle large volumes of data and transactions for many users
options.B: A supercomputer handles transactions; a mainframe performs scientific calculations
options.D: A supercomputer is smaller than a mainframe

questions.explanation: A supercomputer is a very high-performance computer designed for extremely demanding calculations, simulations and large-scale scientific workloads. A mainframe is a powerful computer system designed to handle large volumes of data and transactions for many users and applications with high reliability.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.chapter: Cyber Safety and Responsible Use of IT
questions.question: What is the difference between a hacker and a cracker?

options.A: A hacker explores and tests systems, sometimes ethically; a cracker breaks into systems with malicious intent
options.B: A hacker has malicious intent; a cracker explores systems ethically
options.D: A hacker is for hardware; a cracker is for software

questions.explanation: A hacker explores and tests systems, sometimes ethically (white-hat hacking). A cracker breaks into systems with malicious intent.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between TCP and IP?

options.A: TCP provides reliable, ordered delivery of data; IP provides addressing and packet routing across interconnected networks
options.B: TCP provides addressing; IP provides reliable delivery
options.D: TCP is for wireless only; IP is for wired only

questions.explanation: TCP stands for Transmission Control Protocol. It provides reliable, ordered and error-checked delivery of a byte stream between applications. IP stands for Internet Protocol. It provides addressing and packet routing across interconnected networks.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between vendor lock-in and a Service Level Agreement (SLA)?

options.A: Vendor lock-in occurs when dependence on a provider makes migration difficult; an SLA defines agreed service expectations such as availability and support
options.B: Vendor lock-in defines service expectations; an SLA makes migration difficult
options.D: Vendor lock-in is for storage only; SLA is for computing only

questions.explanation: Vendor lock-in occurs when dependence on a provider's proprietary technologies, services or data formats makes migration to another provider difficult or expensive. A cloud SLA defines agreed service expectations such as availability, support, performance, security responsibilities and remedies for failure.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between 3G and 4G mobile technology?

options.A: 3G improved mobile data capabilities and supported mobile internet and video calling; 4G is designed for high-speed packet-based data communication
options.B: 3G is for high-speed data; 4G is for voice only
options.D: 3G is for text messaging; 4G is for video calling only

questions.explanation: 3G refers to third-generation mobile networks that improved mobile data capabilities and supported services such as mobile internet and video calling. 4G refers to fourth-generation mobile networks designed for high-speed packet-based data communication; LTE is the major technology widely marketed as 4G.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between guided and unguided media?

options.A: Guided media carry signals through a physical path; unguided media transmit signals through free space using electromagnetic waves
options.B: Guided media use radio waves; unguided media use cables
options.D: Guided media are wireless; unguided media are wired

questions.explanation: Guided media carry signals through a physical path, such as twisted-pair cable, coaxial cable and optical fibre. Unguided media transmit signals through free space using electromagnetic waves, such as radio, microwave and infrared signals.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a transaction and a query?

options.A: A transaction is a logical unit of database work treated as a single unit; a query is a request for data or an operation on data
options.B: A transaction requests data; a query performs database operations
options.D: A transaction is for cloud only; a query is for local only

questions.explanation: A transaction is a logical unit of database work that may contain one or more operations and is treated as a single unit for consistency and reliability. A query is a request for data or an operation on data in a database, often expressed using SQL.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between an analogue computer and a digital computer?

options.A: An analogue computer processes continuously varying physical quantities; a digital computer processes data represented in discrete form, usually binary digits 0 and 1
options.B: An analogue computer uses binary digits; a digital computer uses continuous quantities
options.D: An analogue computer is for graphics; a digital computer is for text

questions.explanation: An analogue computer processes continuously varying physical quantities, such as temperature, pressure or voltage. A digital computer processes data represented in discrete form, usually binary digits 0 and 1.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.chapter: Cyber Safety and Responsible Use of IT
questions.question: What is the difference between confidentiality and integrity in information security?

options.A: Confidentiality ensures information is accessible only to authorised parties; integrity ensures information is accurate and not altered without authorisation
options.B: Confidentiality ensures accuracy; integrity ensures access control
options.D: Confidentiality is for hardware; integrity is for software

questions.explanation: Confidentiality ensures information is accessible only to authorised parties. Integrity ensures information is accurate and not altered without authorisation. The three pillars of information security are Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between SMTP and FTP?

options.A: SMTP is used to send and relay email; FTP is designed for transferring files between a client and server
options.B: SMTP transfers files; FTP sends email
options.D: SMTP is for cloud only; FTP is for local only

questions.explanation: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol is used to send and relay email between mail clients and servers or between mail servers. File Transfer Protocol is a network protocol designed for transferring files between a client and server.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a smartphone and a feature phone?

options.A: A smartphone has advanced computing capabilities, an operating system, internet connectivity and the ability to run applications; a feature phone has limited functionality
options.B: A smartphone has limited functionality; a feature phone has advanced capabilities
options.D: A smartphone is for calls only; a feature phone is for apps only

questions.explanation: A smartphone is a mobile phone with advanced computing capabilities, an operating system, internet connectivity and the ability to run applications. A feature phone has limited functionality.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between optical fibre and coaxial cable?

options.A: Optical fibre transmits information as pulses of light through glass or plastic strands; coaxial cable uses a central conductor surrounded by insulation and a conductive shield
options.B: Optical fibre uses copper conductors; coaxial cable uses glass fibres
options.D: Optical fibre is for short distances only; coaxial cable is for long distances only

questions.explanation: Optical fibre communication transmits information as pulses of light through thin strands of glass or plastic fibre. Coaxial cable consists of a central conductor surrounded by insulation and a conductive shield, and is used in applications such as cable television and data communication.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a schema and a view in a database?

options.A: A schema is the logical structure or blueprint of a database; a view is a virtual table defined by a query
options.B: A schema is a virtual table; a view is the logical structure
options.D: A schema is for cloud only; a view is for local only

questions.explanation: A database schema is the logical structure or blueprint of a database, including tables, columns, relationships, constraints and other objects. A view is a virtual table defined by a query; it presents selected data from one or more underlying tables.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a hybrid computer and a digital computer?

options.A: A hybrid computer combines features of analogue and digital computers; a digital computer processes data represented in discrete form
options.B: A hybrid computer uses only binary digits; a digital computer uses continuous quantities
options.D: A hybrid computer is for graphics; a digital computer is for text

questions.explanation: A hybrid computer combines features of analogue and digital computers, such as continuous measurement with digital processing. A digital computer processes data represented in discrete form, usually binary digits 0 and 1.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.chapter: Cyber Safety and Responsible Use of IT
questions.question: What is the difference between availability and integrity in information security?

options.A: Availability ensures information and systems are accessible when needed; integrity ensures information is accurate and not altered without authorisation
options.B: Availability ensures accuracy; integrity ensures access when needed
options.D: Availability is for hardware; integrity is for software

questions.explanation: Availability ensures information and systems are accessible when needed. Integrity ensures information is accurate and not altered without authorisation. The three pillars of information security are Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between an intranet and the Internet?

options.A: An intranet is a private network for internal organisational use; the Internet is a global network of interconnected computer networks
options.B: An intranet is public; the Internet is private
options.D: An intranet is for email only; the Internet is for websites only

questions.explanation: An intranet is a private network that uses Internet technologies to share information and resources within an organisation. The Internet is a global network of interconnected computer networks that communicate using the Internet Protocol suite (TCP/IP).

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a hypervisor and a virtual machine?

options.A: A hypervisor creates and manages virtual machines; a virtual machine is a software-based computer environment that runs an operating system and applications
options.B: A hypervisor runs inside a virtual machine; a virtual machine manages hypervisors
options.D: A hypervisor is for storage only; a virtual machine is for computing only

questions.explanation: A hypervisor is software or firmware that creates and manages virtual machines by allocating physical computing resources. A virtual machine is a software-based computer environment that runs an operating system and applications as if it were a physical computer.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between Wi-Fi and mobile data?

options.A: Wi-Fi is a wireless local-area networking technology; mobile data uses cellular networks to provide internet connectivity
options.B: Wi-Fi uses cellular networks; mobile data uses local-area networking
options.D: Wi-Fi is for long-range communication; mobile data is for short-range communication

questions.explanation: Wi-Fi is a family of wireless local-area networking technologies based on IEEE 802.11 standards. Mobile data uses cellular networks to provide internet connectivity.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a modem and a router?

options.A: A modem modulates and demodulates signals to enable data transmission over a communication medium; a router forwards data packets between different networks
options.B: A modem forwards data packets; a router modulates signals
options.D: A modem is for wireless only; a router is for wired only

questions.explanation: A modem is a device or system that performs modulation and demodulation, or equivalent signal adaptation, to enable data transmission over a communication medium. A router forwards data packets between different networks using network-layer addressing and routing information.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between atomicity and durability in a database transaction?

options.A: Atomicity means a transaction is treated as an indivisible unit: either all operations are committed or none are; durability means once a transaction is committed, its changes are preserved even if a subsequent system failure occurs
options.B: Atomicity means changes are preserved after failure; durability means all operations are committed or none
options.D: Atomicity is for cloud only; durability is for local only

questions.explanation: Atomicity means a transaction is treated as an indivisible unit: either all its operations are committed or none are. Durability means that once a transaction is committed, its changes are preserved even if a subsequent system failure occurs, subject to the system's guarantees.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between an integrated circuit and a transistor?

options.A: An integrated circuit is a miniaturised electronic circuit with components fabricated on a semiconductor material; a transistor is a single semiconductor device used for switching and amplification
options.B: An integrated circuit is a single device; a transistor is a circuit with many components
options.D: An integrated circuit is for storage; a transistor is for processing

questions.explanation: An integrated circuit is a miniaturised electronic circuit in which components such as transistors and resistors are fabricated on a semiconductor material. A transistor is a single semiconductor device used for switching and amplification.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.chapter: Cyber Safety and Responsible Use of IT
questions.question: What is the difference between a strong password and a passphrase?

options.A: A strong password is long, unique and difficult to guess; a passphrase is a sequence of words used as a password
options.B: A strong password is a sequence of words; a passphrase is a short password
options.D: A strong password is for email only; a passphrase is for social media only

questions.explanation: A strong password is long, unique and difficult to guess. A passphrase is a sequence of words used as a password, often easier to remember and type.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a client and a server in the client-server model?

options.A: A client requests services or resources; a server processes requests and provides responses
options.B: A client provides responses; a server requests services
options.D: A client is for hardware; a server is for software

questions.explanation: The client-server model is a computing architecture in which client devices or programs request services or resources from a server, which processes requests and provides responses.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a public cloud and a hybrid cloud?

options.A: A public cloud is available for use by the general public or a broad group of customers; a hybrid cloud combines two or more distinct cloud infrastructures
options.B: A public cloud combines multiple clouds; a hybrid cloud is available to the general public
options.D: A public cloud is for one organisation; a hybrid cloud is for the general public

questions.explanation: A public cloud is cloud infrastructure made available for use by the general public or a broad group of customers and operated by a cloud service provider. A hybrid cloud combines two or more distinct cloud infrastructures, such as private and public clouds, that remain separate but are connected to enable data or application portability.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between GPS and NavIC?

options.A: GPS is a satellite-based navigation system operated by the United States; NavIC is India's regional satellite navigation system developed by ISRO
options.B: GPS is India's navigation system; NavIC is operated by the United States
options.D: GPS is for mobile phones only; NavIC is for aircraft only

questions.explanation: GPS stands for Global Positioning System. It is a satellite-based navigation system operated by the United States that provides positioning, navigation and timing services. NavIC stands for Navigation with Indian Constellation. It is India's regional satellite navigation system developed by ISRO, formerly known as IRNSS.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a communication satellite and a navigation satellite?

options.A: A communication satellite relays radio-frequency signals for services such as television, telephone and data; a navigation satellite provides positioning, navigation and timing services
options.B: A communication satellite provides positioning; a navigation satellite relays signals
options.D: A communication satellite is for military use only; a navigation satellite is for civilian use only

questions.explanation: A communication satellite relays radio-frequency signals between distant locations and supports services such as television, telephone, data and broadband connectivity. A navigation satellite provides positioning, navigation and timing services.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between consistency and isolation in a database transaction?

options.A: Consistency means a committed transaction moves the database from one valid state to another; isolation means concurrent transactions are controlled so that their execution does not produce unacceptable interference
options.B: Consistency means transactions are isolated; isolation means transactions maintain valid states
options.D: Consistency is for cloud only; isolation is for local only

questions.explanation: Consistency means a committed transaction moves the database from one valid state to another while preserving defined rules and constraints. Isolation means concurrent transactions are controlled so that their execution does not produce unacceptable interference, according to the database's isolation level.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a register and RAM?

options.A: Registers are very small, high-speed storage locations inside the processor; RAM is the computer's primary working memory used to hold programs and data currently in use
options.B: Registers are larger than RAM; RAM is inside the processor
options.D: Registers are for storage; RAM is for processing

questions.explanation: Registers are very small, high-speed storage locations inside the processor used to hold instructions, addresses, data and intermediate results temporarily. RAM stands for Random Access Memory. It is the computer's primary working memory used to hold programs and data currently in use.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.chapter: Cyber Safety and Responsible Use of IT
questions.question: What is the difference between a vulnerability and an exploit?

options.A: A vulnerability is a weakness in a system; an exploit is a method or code that takes advantage of a vulnerability
options.B: A vulnerability takes advantage of a weakness; an exploit is a weakness in a system
options.D: A vulnerability is for hardware; an exploit is for software

questions.explanation: A vulnerability is a weakness in a system. An exploit is a method or code that takes advantage of a vulnerability.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between an IP address and a MAC address?

options.A: An IP address is a numerical identifier assigned to a network interface for communication using IP; a MAC address is a hardware identifier assigned to a network interface
options.B: An IP address is a hardware identifier; a MAC address is a numerical identifier
options.D: An IP address is for wireless only; a MAC address is for wired only

questions.explanation: An Internet Protocol address is a numerical identifier assigned to a network interface for communication using IP. A MAC address is a hardware identifier assigned to a network interface.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a private cloud and a community cloud?

options.A: A private cloud is provisioned for exclusive use by a single organisation; a community cloud is shared by organisations with common concerns
options.B: A private cloud is shared by multiple organisations; a community cloud is for a single organisation
options.D: A private cloud is public; a community cloud is private

questions.explanation: A private cloud is cloud infrastructure provisioned for exclusive use by a single organisation, though it may be managed by that organisation or a third party. A community cloud is cloud infrastructure shared by organisations with common concerns, such as mission, security requirements, policy or compliance needs.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between Bluetooth and NFC?

options.A: Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology for exchanging data and connecting devices; NFC is a very short-range contactless communication technology
options.B: Bluetooth is for contactless payments; NFC is for device connections
options.D: Bluetooth is for long-range communication; NFC is for medium-range communication

questions.explanation: Bluetooth is a short-range wireless technology used to exchange data and connect devices such as headphones, keyboards, speakers and sensors. NFC is a short-range wireless technology used for contactless communication, including payments and device pairing.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a guided medium and an unguided medium?

options.A: A guided medium carries signals through a physical path; an unguided medium transmits signals through free space using electromagnetic waves
options.B: A guided medium uses radio waves; an unguided medium uses cables
options.D: A guided medium is wireless; an unguided medium is wired

questions.explanation: Guided media carry signals through a physical path, such as twisted-pair cable, coaxial cable and optical fibre. Unguided media transmit signals through free space using electromagnetic waves, such as radio, microwave and infrared signals.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a primary key and a candidate key?

options.A: A primary key is the chosen candidate key that uniquely identifies each row; a candidate key is any minimal set of attributes that can uniquely identify each row
options.B: A primary key is any minimal set; a candidate key is the chosen key
options.D: A primary key is for foreign tables; a candidate key is for primary tables

questions.explanation: A primary key is a column or set of columns that uniquely identifies each row in a table and cannot contain duplicate or null key values. A candidate key is a minimal set of attributes that can uniquely identify each row in a relation.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a mainframe and a minicomputer?

options.A: A mainframe is a powerful computer system designed for large volumes of data and transactions; a minicomputer is a historical class of mid-range multi-user computer smaller than a mainframe
options.B: A mainframe is smaller than a minicomputer; a minicomputer is larger than a mainframe
options.D: A mainframe is for personal use; a minicomputer is for enterprise use

questions.explanation: A mainframe is a powerful computer system designed to handle large volumes of data and transactions for many users and applications with high reliability. A minicomputer is a historical class of mid-range multi-user computer smaller than a mainframe; the term is less common in modern computing.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.chapter: Cyber Safety and Responsible Use of IT
questions.question: What is the difference between a zero-day exploit and a known vulnerability?

options.A: A zero-day exploit targets a vulnerability that is unknown to the vendor or has no patch; a known vulnerability is publicly documented and may have a patch
options.B: A zero-day exploit targets a known vulnerability; a known vulnerability is unknown to the vendor
options.D: A zero-day exploit is for hardware; a known vulnerability is for software

questions.explanation: A zero-day exploit targets a vulnerability that is unknown to the vendor or has no patch. A known vulnerability is publicly documented and may have a patch.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a website and a web application?

options.A: A website is a collection of related web pages and resources; a web application is software accessed through a web browser that provides interactive functionality
options.B: A website provides interactive functionality; a web application is a collection of pages
options.D: A website is for businesses only; a web application is for individuals only

questions.explanation: A website is a collection of related web pages and resources generally published under a common domain name. A web application is software accessed through a web browser that provides interactive functionality.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a cloud provider and a cloud customer?

options.A: A cloud provider operates and manages cloud infrastructure and services; a cloud customer uses cloud services
options.B: A cloud provider uses cloud services; a cloud customer operates cloud infrastructure
options.D: A cloud provider is for storage only; a cloud customer is for computing only

questions.explanation: A cloud provider operates and manages cloud infrastructure and services. A cloud customer uses cloud services.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a mobile network operator and a mobile virtual network operator (MVNO)?

options.A: A mobile network operator owns and operates cellular infrastructure; an MVNO uses another operator's infrastructure to provide services
options.B: A mobile network operator uses another operator's infrastructure; an MVNO owns cellular infrastructure
options.D: A mobile network operator is for 5G only; an MVNO is for 2G only

questions.explanation: A mobile network operator owns and operates cellular infrastructure. A mobile virtual network operator (MVNO) uses another operator's infrastructure to provide services.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a signal and a carrier?

options.A: A signal carries information; a carrier is a waveform that is modulated to carry information
options.B: A signal is a waveform that is modulated; a carrier carries information
options.D: A signal is for wireless only; a carrier is for wired only

questions.explanation: A signal carries information. A carrier is a waveform that is modulated to carry information.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a relation and a table in a relational database?

options.A: A relation is a mathematical concept representing a set of tuples; a table is the physical implementation of a relation in a relational database
options.B: A relation is a physical table; a table is a mathematical concept
options.D: A relation is for cloud only; a table is for local only

questions.explanation: A relation is a mathematical concept representing a set of tuples. A table is the physical implementation of a relation in a relational database.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a motherboard and a CPU?

options.A: A motherboard is the main printed circuit board that connects components; a CPU is the principal processor that executes instructions
options.B: A motherboard executes instructions; a CPU connects components
options.D: A motherboard is for storage; a CPU is for processing

questions.explanation: The motherboard is the main printed circuit board of a computer. It connects the CPU, memory, storage, expansion cards and input/output components. The CPU is the principal processor of a computer. It executes instructions, performs calculations and controls the operation of other components.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.chapter: Cyber Safety and Responsible Use of IT
questions.question: What is the difference between a phishing attack and a social engineering attack?

options.A: Phishing is a type of social engineering that uses fraudulent messages to trick users; social engineering is the broader manipulation of people to reveal information or perform actions
options.B: Phishing is a broader term; social engineering is a type of phishing
options.D: Phishing is for hardware; social engineering is for software

questions.explanation: Phishing is a type of social engineering that uses fraudulent messages to trick users into revealing information or performing actions. Social engineering is the broader manipulation of people into revealing confidential information or performing actions that compromise security.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a domain name and a hostname?

options.A: A domain name identifies an internet resource or network location; a hostname identifies a specific device within a domain
options.B: A domain name identifies a device; a hostname identifies a network location
options.D: A domain name is for email only; a hostname is for websites only

questions.explanation: A domain name is a human-readable name used to identify an internet resource or network location, such as example.com. A hostname identifies a specific device within a domain.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a mobile browser and a mobile app?

options.A: A mobile browser is software used to access web content; a mobile app is software designed to run natively on a mobile device
options.B: A mobile browser is installed software; a mobile app is accessed through a browser
options.D: A mobile browser is for Android only; a mobile app is for iOS only

questions.explanation: A mobile browser is application software used to access, retrieve and display web pages. A mobile app is software designed to run on a mobile device such as a smartphone or tablet.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a baseband signal and a broadband signal?

options.A: A baseband signal uses a single frequency band; a broadband signal uses multiple frequency bands to carry data
options.B: A baseband signal uses multiple bands; a broadband signal uses a single band
options.D: A baseband signal is for wireless only; a broadband signal is for wired only

questions.explanation: A baseband signal uses a single frequency band. A broadband signal uses multiple frequency bands to carry data.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a table and a relation in a relational database?

options.A: A table is the physical implementation of a relation; a relation is a mathematical concept representing a set of tuples
options.B: A table is a mathematical concept; a relation is a physical implementation
options.D: A table is for cloud only; a relation is for local only

questions.explanation: A table is a structured collection of related records arranged in rows and columns. A relation is a mathematical concept representing a set of tuples.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a peripheral device and an internal component?

options.A: A peripheral device is connected externally to a computer to provide input, output, storage or communication functions; an internal component is located inside the computer case
options.B: A peripheral device is inside the computer; an internal component is connected externally
options.D: A peripheral device is for storage; an internal component is for processing

questions.explanation: A peripheral device is a hardware component connected to a computer to provide input, output, storage or communication functions. An internal component is located inside the computer case, such as the CPU, motherboard and RAM.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.chapter: Cyber Safety and Responsible Use of IT
questions.question: What is the difference between a firewall and a proxy server?

options.A: A firewall monitors and filters network traffic according to defined rules; a proxy server acts as an intermediary between clients and servers
options.B: A firewall acts as an intermediary; a proxy server filters network traffic
options.D: A firewall is for hardware only; a proxy server is for software only

questions.explanation: A firewall is a hardware or software security control that monitors and filters network traffic according to defined rules. A proxy server acts as an intermediary between clients and servers.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between IPv4 and IPv6?

options.A: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses; IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses and provides a vastly larger address space
options.B: IPv4 uses 128-bit addresses; IPv6 uses 32-bit addresses
options.D: IPv4 is for wireless only; IPv6 is for wired only

questions.explanation: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses, commonly written in dotted-decimal form; IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses, written in hexadecimal groups, and provides a vastly larger address space.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a cloud data centre and a traditional data centre?

options.A: A cloud data centre supports cloud services with virtualisation and resource pooling; a traditional data centre typically hosts dedicated physical servers
options.B: A cloud data centre hosts dedicated servers; a traditional data centre supports virtualisation
options.D: A cloud data centre is for storage only; a traditional data centre is for computing only

questions.explanation: A data centre is the physical facility containing servers, storage, networking, power and cooling systems that support cloud services. A traditional data centre typically hosts dedicated physical servers.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a mobile operating system and a desktop operating system?

options.A: A mobile operating system is designed for mobile devices such as smartphones and tablets; a desktop operating system is designed for desktop and laptop computers
options.B: A mobile operating system is for desktops; a desktop operating system is for mobile devices
options.D: A mobile operating system is for Android only; a desktop operating system is for Windows only

questions.explanation: Android and Apple's iOS are major mobile operating systems. Microsoft Windows, macOS and Linux distributions are examples of desktop operating systems.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a digital signal and an analogue signal?

options.A: A digital signal uses discrete values; an analogue signal varies continuously
options.B: A digital signal varies continuously; an analogue signal uses discrete values
options.D: A digital signal is for wireless only; an analogue signal is for wired only

questions.explanation: A digital signal uses discrete values, commonly binary bits. An analogue signal varies continuously.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a row and a column in a relational database?

options.A: A row represents one individual entry in a table; a column represents a particular attribute of the records
options.B: A row represents an attribute; a column represents an entry
options.D: A row is for storage; a column is for processing

questions.explanation: A record or row represents one individual entry in a table, containing values for the table's fields. A field or column represents a particular attribute of the records in a table, such as name, date or application number.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a storage device and a memory device?

options.A: A storage device retains data over time; a memory device holds data temporarily for processing
options.B: A storage device holds data temporarily; a memory device retains data over time
options.D: A storage device is for cloud only; a memory device is for local only

questions.explanation: Secondary storage is non-volatile storage used to retain data and programs over time. RAM is the computer's primary working memory used to hold programs and data currently in use.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.chapter: Cyber Safety and Responsible Use of IT
questions.question: What is the difference between a software update and a security patch?

options.A: A software update may include new features, improvements and fixes; a security patch specifically addresses a security vulnerability
options.B: A software update addresses security vulnerabilities; a security patch adds new features
options.D: A software update is for hardware; a security patch is for software

questions.explanation: A software update may include new features, improvements and fixes. A security patch specifically addresses a security vulnerability.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a web protocol and a mail protocol?

options.A: A web protocol such as HTTP is used for transferring web resources; a mail protocol such as SMTP, POP3 or IMAP is used for email
options.B: A web protocol is used for email; a mail protocol is used for web browsing
options.D: A web protocol is for cloud only; a mail protocol is for local only

questions.explanation: HTTP is an application-layer protocol used for transferring web resources between clients and servers. SMTP is used to send and relay email; POP3 and IMAP are used to retrieve or synchronise email.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a cloud application and a traditional application?

options.A: A cloud application is accessed over a network and often runs on cloud infrastructure; a traditional application is installed and run on local devices
options.B: A cloud application is installed locally; a traditional application is accessed over a network
options.D: A cloud application is for storage only; a traditional application is for computing only

questions.explanation: SaaS provides ready-to-use software applications over a network, usually through a browser or app, while the provider manages the application and underlying infrastructure. A traditional application is installed and run on local devices.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a mobile payment and a digital wallet?

options.A: A mobile payment is a payment initiated or completed using a mobile device; a digital wallet is a service that stores payment information and enables transactions
options.B: A mobile payment stores payment information; a digital wallet initiates payments
options.D: A mobile payment is for businesses only; a digital wallet is for individuals only

questions.explanation: A mobile payment is a payment initiated or completed using a mobile device, through methods such as UPI apps, NFC wallets, QR codes or mobile banking. A digital wallet is a service that stores payment information and enables transactions.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a packet and a frame?

options.A: A packet is a unit of data at the network layer; a frame is a unit of data at the data link layer
options.B: A packet is at the data link layer; a frame is at the network layer
options.D: A packet is for wireless only; a frame is for wired only

questions.explanation: A packet is a unit of data at the network layer. A frame is a unit of data at the data link layer.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a database and a spreadsheet?

options.A: A database is designed to store, manage and query large volumes of structured data; a spreadsheet is primarily used for calculations and simple data organisation
options.B: A database is for calculations; a spreadsheet is for large-scale data management
options.D: A database is for cloud only; a spreadsheet is for local only

questions.explanation: A database is an organised collection of related data stored and managed so that it can be accessed, retrieved, updated and analysed efficiently. A spreadsheet is primarily used for calculations and simple data organisation.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a hard disk drive and a USB flash drive?

options.A: A hard disk drive uses rotating magnetic platters; a USB flash drive uses flash memory and connects through a USB interface
options.B: A hard disk drive uses flash memory; a USB flash drive uses magnetic platters
options.D: A hard disk drive is portable; a USB flash drive is internal

questions.explanation: An HDD stores data magnetically on rotating platters and uses mechanical read/write components. A USB flash drive is a portable, non-volatile storage device that uses flash memory and connects through a Universal Serial Bus interface.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.chapter: Cyber Safety and Responsible Use of IT
questions.question: What is the difference between a privacy policy and a security policy?

options.A: A privacy policy explains how personal information is collected, used and protected; a security policy defines rules and procedures for protecting systems and data
options.B: A privacy policy defines security rules; a security policy explains data collection
options.D: A privacy policy is for cloud only; a security policy is for local only

questions.explanation: A privacy policy explains how personal information is collected, used and protected. A security policy defines rules and procedures for protecting systems and data.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a web server and an application server?

options.A: A web server delivers web content using protocols such as HTTP; an application server provides business logic and application services
options.B: A web server provides business logic; an application server delivers web content
options.D: A web server is for email only; an application server is for websites only

questions.explanation: A web server is software and/or a computer system that stores, processes and delivers web content or services to clients using protocols such as HTTP. An application server provides business logic and application services.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a cloud region and a cloud availability zone?

options.A: A cloud region is a geographic area containing multiple data centres; an availability zone is an isolated location within a region
options.B: A cloud region is an isolated location; an availability zone is a geographic area
options.D: A cloud region is for storage only; an availability zone is for computing only

questions.explanation: A cloud region is a geographic area containing multiple data centres. An availability zone is an isolated location within a region.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a mobile network and a Wi-Fi network?

options.A: A mobile network uses cellular infrastructure to provide wide-area coverage; a Wi-Fi network provides local-area wireless connectivity
options.B: A mobile network provides local-area coverage; a Wi-Fi network provides wide-area coverage
options.D: A mobile network is for data only; a Wi-Fi network is for voice only

questions.explanation: A mobile network is a wireless telecommunications system that connects mobile devices to voice, messaging and data services through radio access infrastructure and a core network. Wi-Fi is a family of wireless local-area networking technologies based on IEEE 802.11 standards.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a transmitter and a receiver?

options.A: A transmitter sends information through a communication channel; a receiver receives and processes the information
options.B: A transmitter receives information; a receiver sends information
options.D: A transmitter is for wireless only; a receiver is for wired only

questions.explanation: A communication system transfers information from a source to a destination through a transmitter, communication channel and receiver. The transmitter sends information; the receiver receives and processes it.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a database and a file system?

options.A: A database is an organised collection of related data managed by a DBMS; a file system is the method an operating system uses to organise and store files
options.B: A database is a method for organising files; a file system is an organised collection of data
options.D: A database is for cloud only; a file system is for local only

questions.explanation: A database is an organised collection of related data stored and managed so that it can be accessed, retrieved, updated and analysed efficiently. A file system is the method and data structure an operating system uses to organise, name, store and retrieve files on storage media.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a power supply unit (PSU) and a battery?

options.A: A PSU converts electrical power from an external source into regulated power for computer components; a battery stores electrical energy
options.B: A PSU stores electrical energy; a battery converts electrical power
options.D: A PSU is for laptops only; a battery is for desktops only

questions.explanation: A PSU converts electrical power from an external source into regulated power suitable for computer components. A battery stores electrical energy.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.chapter: Cyber Safety and Responsible Use of IT
questions.question: What is the difference between a password manager and a browser's built-in password saver?

options.A: A password manager is dedicated software for creating and storing unique passwords securely; a browser's built-in password saver stores passwords within the browser
options.B: A password manager stores passwords in the browser; a browser's password saver is dedicated software
options.D: A password manager is for hardware only; a browser's password saver is for software only

questions.explanation: A password manager is dedicated software that helps create and store unique passwords for different services securely. A browser's built-in password saver stores passwords within the browser.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a secure protocol and an insecure protocol?

options.A: A secure protocol uses encryption and authentication to protect communication; an insecure protocol does not provide these protections
options.B: A secure protocol is faster than an insecure protocol
options.D: A secure protocol is for email only; an insecure protocol is for websites only

questions.explanation: HTTPS protects HTTP communication using TLS, helping prevent eavesdropping and tampering and allowing the client to authenticate the server. HTTP by itself does not provide these protections.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between cloud migration and cloud adoption?

options.A: Cloud migration is the process of moving data and applications to the cloud; cloud adoption is the broader process of integrating cloud services into an organisation
options.B: Cloud migration is integrating cloud services; cloud adoption is moving data to the cloud
options.D: Cloud migration is for storage only; cloud adoption is for computing only

questions.explanation: Cloud migration is the process of moving data and applications to the cloud. Cloud adoption is the broader process of integrating cloud services into an organisation.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a mobile hotspot and tethering?

options.A: A mobile hotspot is a feature that shares a mobile device's internet connection with other devices; tethering is the general term for sharing a mobile device's internet connection
options.B: A mobile hotspot is a general term; tethering is a specific feature
options.D: A mobile hotspot is for Android only; tethering is for iOS only

questions.explanation: A mobile hotspot is a feature that shares a mobile device's internet connection with other devices. Tethering is the general term for sharing a mobile device's internet connection.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a data rate and a baud rate?

options.A: A data rate is the number of bits transmitted per second; a baud rate is the number of signal changes per second
options.B: A data rate is the number of signal changes; a baud rate is the number of bits
options.D: A data rate is for wireless only; a baud rate is for wired only

questions.explanation: A data rate is the number of bits transmitted per second. A baud rate is the number of signal changes per second.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a relational database and a NoSQL database?

options.A: A relational database organises data into tables with relationships through keys; a NoSQL database uses non-relational data models such as document, key-value, wide-column or graph
options.B: A relational database uses non-relational models; a NoSQL database uses tables and keys
options.D: A relational database is for cloud only; a NoSQL database is for local only

questions.explanation: A relational database organises data into tables consisting of rows and columns, with relationships between tables represented through keys. NoSQL refers to database systems that use data models other than, or in addition to, the traditional relational table model, including document, key-value, wide-column and graph databases.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a cooling fan and a heat sink?

options.A: A cooling fan moves air to dissipate heat; a heat sink is a passive component that absorbs and dissipates heat
options.B: A cooling fan absorbs heat; a heat sink moves air
options.D: A cooling fan is for storage only; a heat sink is for processing only

questions.explanation: A cooling fan moves air to dissipate heat. A heat sink is a passive component that absorbs and dissipates heat.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.chapter: Cyber Safety and Responsible Use of IT
questions.question: What is the difference between a digital certificate and a digital signature?

options.A: A digital certificate binds a public key to an identity; a digital signature verifies the authenticity and integrity of a message or document
options.B: A digital certificate verifies message integrity; a digital signature binds a public key
options.D: A digital certificate is for email only; a digital signature is for websites only

questions.explanation: A digital certificate binds a public key to an identity. A digital signature helps authenticate the signer and verify that an electronic message or document has not been altered after signing.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a stateless protocol and a stateful protocol?

options.A: A stateless protocol does not retain session state between requests; a stateful protocol retains session state
options.B: A stateless protocol retains session state; a stateful protocol does not
options.D: A stateless protocol is for email only; a stateful protocol is for websites only

questions.explanation: A stateless protocol does not retain session state between requests. A stateful protocol retains session state. HTTP is a stateless protocol.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a cloud service provider and a cloud broker?

options.A: A cloud service provider offers cloud services; a cloud broker manages the use, performance and delivery of cloud services between providers and consumers
options.B: A cloud service provider manages services between providers; a cloud broker offers cloud services
options.D: A cloud service provider is for storage only; a cloud broker is for computing only

questions.explanation: A cloud service provider offers cloud services. A cloud broker manages the use, performance and delivery of cloud services between providers and consumers.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a physical topology and a logical topology?

options.A: A physical topology describes the physical layout of network devices and cables; a logical topology describes how data flows through the network
options.B: A physical topology describes data flow; a logical topology describes physical layout
options.D: A physical topology is for wireless only; a logical topology is for wired only

questions.explanation: A physical topology describes the physical layout of network devices and cables. A logical topology describes how data flows through the network.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a database trigger and a stored procedure?

options.A: A trigger automatically executes in response to a specified event; a stored procedure is explicitly called to perform a task
options.B: A trigger is explicitly called; a stored procedure automatically executes
options.D: A trigger is for cloud only; a stored procedure is for local only

questions.explanation: A trigger automatically executes in response to a specified event. A stored procedure is explicitly called to perform a task.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a BIOS and a UEFI?

options.A: BIOS is a basic input/output system firmware; UEFI is a modern firmware interface that replaces BIOS with additional features
options.B: BIOS is a modern firmware interface; UEFI is a basic input/output system
options.D: BIOS is for storage only; UEFI is for processing only

questions.explanation: BIOS stands for Basic Input/Output System. UEFI is a modern firmware interface that replaces BIOS with additional features.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.chapter: Cyber Safety and Responsible Use of IT
questions.question: What is the difference between a data controller and a data processor?

options.A: A data controller determines the purposes and means of processing personal data; a data processor processes personal data on behalf of a controller
options.B: A data controller processes data on behalf of a processor; a data processor determines purposes
options.D: A data controller is for hardware only; a data processor is for software only

questions.explanation: A data controller determines the purposes and means of processing personal data. A data processor processes personal data on behalf of a controller.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a URI and a URL?

options.A: A URI is a broad identifier for a resource; a URL is a specific type of URI that provides the location of a resource
options.B: A URI provides location; a URL is a broad identifier
options.D: A URI is for email only; a URL is for websites only

questions.explanation: A URI (Uniform Resource Identifier) is a broad identifier for a resource. A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is a specific type of URI that provides the location of a resource.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between cloud elasticity and cloud scalability?

options.A: Elasticity is the ability to scale resources up or down quickly in response to demand; scalability is the ability to handle growing workloads by adding resources
options.B: Elasticity is the ability to add resources; scalability is the ability to scale quickly
options.D: Elasticity is for storage only; scalability is for computing only

questions.explanation: Rapid elasticity means cloud resources can be scaled up or down quickly in response to changing demand. Scalability is the ability to handle growing workloads by adding resources.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a mobile OS update and a security patch?

options.A: A mobile OS update may include new features and improvements; a security patch specifically addresses security vulnerabilities
options.B: A mobile OS update addresses security vulnerabilities; a security patch adds new features
options.D: A mobile OS update is for hardware; a security patch is for software

questions.explanation: A mobile OS update may include new features and improvements. A security patch specifically addresses security vulnerabilities.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a network protocol and a network standard?

options.A: A protocol is a set of agreed rules for communication; a standard is a documented norm or specification that may define protocols
options.B: A protocol is a documented norm; a standard is a set of rules
options.D: A protocol is for wireless only; a standard is for wired only

questions.explanation: A protocol is a set of agreed rules that define how devices format, transmit, receive and interpret data. A standard is a documented norm or specification that may define protocols.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a database administrator and a data analyst?

options.A: A database administrator manages database installation, configuration, security, performance, backup and recovery; a data analyst interprets data to support decision-making
options.B: A database administrator interprets data; a data analyst manages databases
options.D: A database administrator is for cloud only; a data analyst is for local only

questions.explanation: A DBA is a professional responsible for database installation, configuration, security, performance, backup, recovery and ongoing administration. A data analyst interprets data to support decision-making.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a graphics card and a GPU?

options.A: A graphics card is an expansion card that contains a GPU and other components; a GPU is the processor designed to accelerate graphics and parallel computations
options.B: A graphics card is a processor; a GPU is an expansion card
options.D: A graphics card is for storage only; a GPU is for processing only

questions.explanation: A graphics card is an expansion card that contains a GPU and other components. A GPU is a processor designed to accelerate graphics and highly parallel computations.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.chapter: Cyber Safety and Responsible Use of IT
questions.question: What is the difference between a password and a PIN?

options.A: A password is typically a longer string of characters; a PIN is a numeric code often used for authentication
options.B: A password is numeric; a PIN is alphanumeric
options.D: A password is for hardware only; a PIN is for software only

questions.explanation: A password is typically a longer string of characters. A PIN is a numeric code often used for authentication.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a GET request and a POST request in HTTP?

options.A: GET retrieves data from a server; POST sends data to a server to create or update a resource
options.B: GET sends data to a server; POST retrieves data
options.D: GET is for email only; POST is for websites only

questions.explanation: GET retrieves data from a server. POST sends data to a server to create or update a resource.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between cloud computing and edge computing?

options.A: Cloud computing processes data in centralised data centres; edge computing processes data closer to the source of data generation
options.B: Cloud computing processes data at the edge; edge computing processes data in centralised data centres
options.D: Cloud computing is for storage only; edge computing is for computing only

questions.explanation: Cloud computing processes data in centralised data centres. Edge computing processes data closer to the source of data generation.

questions.subject: Information Technology
questions.question: What is the difference between a mobile payment app and a mobile banking app?
